people.name: Linda Storli
people.archive_holds: Person #25157 (no body, no occupation). Hart holdings #28612 (Trustee Area 1, 2015-12 to 2020-12, elected) and #28614 (2020-12 to 2024-12, elected, howEnded expired; she lost on November 5, 2024). Candidacies: Hart Area 1 2015, 2020, 2024; City Council 1987, 1992, 1994. Named in article #26999 ("The ladder that runs the other way").
public_life_beyond_the_board: Canyon High School teacher for 30 years (her own statements and press); retired from teaching in 2015.
Member of the City of Santa Clarita's first Parks and Recreation Commission (1988 to 1990 on Leon Worden's commissioners list); by her own bio, on the city formation committee of 1987.
Stood for the City Council in 1987, 1992 and 1994 (archive candidacies).
Realtor (ballot designation "Teacher/Realtor", 2015).

Board president for 2020 (the year of COVID-19 closures and the Saugus High shooting remembrances) and for 2024; spoke for the 2021 decision to retire the Hart High Indian mascot and the 2024 reveal of the Hart Hawks.
people.board_service_and_disagreements: Elected 2015 (Area 1, defeating incumbent Mercado-Fortine), re-elected 2020, lost 2024 (third of three, behind Aakash Ahuja and Mercado-Fortine). Officer years: Assistant Clerk 2018, Clerk 2019 and 2023, President 2020 and 2024. No disagreement on the terms. Minor: election-night counts (SCVNews 1,193 to 913) differ from the CEDA canvass (1,428 to 1,078) for 2015.

people.name: Paul Strickland
people.archive_holds: Person #25425 (no body). Holdings: Sulphur Springs #28233 (1995-12 to 1999-12, elected) and Hart #28235 (2001-12 to 2013-05-01, elected, resigned), both footnoted to the 2013 district release on SCVNews. Candidacies: Sulphur Springs 1995; Hart 1999 (lost), 2001, 2005, 2009. Named in article #26999. Note: district-boards-check-2026-10-04 lists #25425 as an open Sulphur Springs holding; the probe of 5 October shows it closed (1999-12, expired).
public_life_beyond_the_board: Trustee of the Sulphur Springs Union School District, 1995 to 1999.
City of Santa Clarita Arts Commission from December 2009, its chairman in 2012 and 2013; earlier president of the Santa Clarita Arts Advisory Committee (his own 2005 statement).

Republican candidate for the 38th Assembly District in the June 2012 primary (14.7 percent, fourth), endorsed by the California Teachers Association; at the time field deputy to Assemblyman Cameron Smyth.

Animation producer by profession (ballot designations 1995 to 2001); actor with the Canyon Theatre Guild; Measure V and SA bond committees; Open Space Commission member; co-chair of the Hart diversity committee; opponent of the Cemex mine (district release, 2013).
Not related to State Senator Tony Strickland (SCVNews, 2011): the 2014 congressional race "Strickland, Knight" is Tony Strickland and is not his.
people.board_service_and_disagreements: Sulphur Springs 1995-1999; lost a Hart race in 1999; Hart 2001 to May 1, 2013 (resigned to move out of state); president 2005-06 and 2009-10 (roster). Disagreement: the roster prints, on the 2013-14 board, "Paul B. Strickland (relected/unopposed 2013 due to timing of filing period; did not assume office)", while the County's list of candidates not on the November 5, 2013 ballot (already footnoted on #29627) names Chris A. Fall, "Appointed Incumbent", for that seat, and SCVNews reports Fall as the filer. Footnote both; state neither.

people.name: Steven Sturgeon
people.archive_holds: Person #25441 (no body). Hart holdings #28630 (1999-2003), #28632, #28634, #28636, #28638 (Trustee Area 4, 2015-12 to 2020-12, lost November 3, 2020). Candidacies 1999 to 2020. No Sulphur Springs holding, though his own statements put him on that board 1994 to 1999.
public_life_beyond_the_board: Trustee of the Sulphur Springs Union School District, "94-99" (his 2003 Smart Voter statement; his 1999 ballot designation was "Governing Board Member/Sulphur Springs Union School District").
2013 Santa Clarita Valley Man of the Year (nominated by the SCV Child & Family Center and the Rotary Club of SCV); co-chaired the 2014 event.
California School Boards Association delegate; director of the Los Angeles County School Trustees Association; SCV Facilities Foundation representative for the board (2014).
Business: software (MBA Systems; AVM Technologies, Inc.) and Confidential Data Destruction Company (his statements and the 2013 award biography).
In 2014, as the board voted 4-1 to move to trustee areas under the California Voting Rights Act, he explained the move to the press.
people.board_service_and_disagreements: Hart 1999 to December 2020, 21 years; president four times (2003-04, 2008-09, 2014, 2018 per roster and SCVNews: "fourth time"). Lost Area 4 to James Webb in 2020. Disagreement: the mirror's people.htm lists him under "2012: SCV Man & Woman of the Year"; mwoty.htm and SCVNews (May 4, 2013) say 2013. The contemporary report rules: 2013.
